extractions.title: I Blame My Father's Summer Reading Lists
key_claims: The author's major life choices, including a 15,000-mile solo road trip across America at age 27, can be traced back to summer reading lists assigned by her father.

Her father, a professor of French and Francophone literature, gave her books far beyond her emotional comprehension, including Nabokov's Lolita at age 12 and works by Anaïs Nin, Paul Bowles, Fanon, Flaubert, Kafka, Camus, and Sartre.
Reading Isabelle Eberhardt's 'The Passionate Nomad' at age 14 profoundly shaped the author's relationship with the desert and her desire for freedom and exploration.
The author's father has just published a biography titled 'The Immortal Journeys of Isabelle Eberhardt.'

The author later traced versions of Isabelle Eberhardt's journeys through North Africa, including studying in Morocco's Atlas Mountains, gathering oral histories in Tunisia, studying in Alexandria, and taking camping trips into the Sahara and other desert regions.
